subject: CS Handoff: Modeling scope & token footprint for Praxis Health
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@praxishealth.com>, Mike Antonucci <mike@praxishealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CS Handoff: Modeling scope & token footprint for Praxis Health

Hi Elena + Mike —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. This thread is the CS <> Solutions handoff focused on the model selection and workload sizing we discussed. I want to capture what we think will be the short-term serving plan and a few open questions to lock before implementation.

Summary (proposal):
- Model shortlist: a) Mistral-7B-instruct (FP16 baseline), b) LlamaX-13B-ggml-q4_0 (quantized variant for cost-sensitive endpoints), c) Claude-2-mini for high-safety, low-latency routing.
- Context length: primary UX path requires 8k context for a single conversational session (most prompts are ~600 tokens + up to 6k of user & doc context in retrieval-augmented flows). We propose reserving a 8k KV-profile and testing a 16k fallback for long-doc uploads.
- Traffic profile & token estimates (starting point): average request: 1,300 prompt tokens, 700 response tokens; peak concurrent users: 40 active sessions; peak RPS for API surface: 25 rps. Estimated monthly token volume (30d ramp): ~300M input tokens / ~160M output tokens -> ~460M total tokens.
- Deployment suggestion: start on Redwood Hosted with a model mix (Mistral-7B + quantized LlamaX) and enable dedicated capacity if 95th-percentile latency or cost targets are breached.

Open questions for Praxis:
1) What fraction of requests will include full document retrieval vs. short prompts? (helps determine context cache hit rate)
2) Do you expect high fan-out (one user -> many API calls) during ingestion or mostly single-call flows?
3) Is there any regulatory constraint requiring private deployment or particular data residency?

Next steps I propose:
- Quick alignment call next week (30m) to validate the token estimates and finalize the shortlist.
- Shared MA Plan and prompt samples attached (mutual_action_plan.xlsx, example_prompt_samples.txt).
- Engineering kickoff: once shortlist confirmed, Solutions will run a two-week perf sweep with sample traffic and provide throughput/latency CSVs and a recommended pod size.

Please reply with any immediate corrections to the assumptions above. If the traffic numbers look off, tell us the expected daily active users and avg message size and we'll recompute.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Elena Torres <elena@praxishealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Antonucci <mike@praxishealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 11:06:00 -0400
Subject: Re: CS Handoff: Modeling scope & token footprint for Praxis Health

Jordan —

Thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Document mix: roughly 60% short prompts (single documents or short form Q/A), ~30% RAG where we attach one clinical note (4–8k tokens), and ~10% multi-doc uploads (longer clinical histories).
- Fan-out: ingestion pipeline does a small-batch fan-out — typically 1 user -> 2–3 retrieval calls during enrichment, so plan for modest fan-out.
- Regulatory: we are fine with hosted for the POC, but production will require a VPC/private deployment and will need to pass our security review (SOC-like checklist provided).

I'll attach the product API spec (praxis_product_api_spec.pdf) and a short traffic snapshot for last month. Our initial target SLA is 300ms p50 for interactive flows; we can tolerate 1s p95 for RAG endpoints.

Can we add a short bullet to the MA plan for data purging/retention expectations? We keep 90 days of conversational context by default.

Elena
Director, Product — Praxis Health
elena@praxishealth.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@praxishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mike Antonucci <mike@praxishealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Aug 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CS Handoff: Modeling scope & token footprint for Praxis Health

Jordan / Elena —

Quick addition from Solutions: given Elena's 60/30/10 doc mix and the 2–3 call fan-out, I recommend we:
- Start benchmarking with an 8k KV profile and a 16k model variant queued as a cold fallback. The 16k path can be routed to a higher-cost pool only for multi-doc uploads.
- For token budgeting, we'll assume an effective inflation factor of 1.15 to account for metadata and retrieval vectors (so the estimated 460M becomes ~529M billing tokens).
- Run a 72-hour load sweep with synthetic RAG traffic to validate cache hit ratios; we'll include telemetry hooks for prefix cache hit/miss and per-request token accounting.

I've updated the MA plan with those notes and added a section recommending the initial pod sizing (2 x g5.12xlarge-equivalent for the baseline mix).

Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@praxishealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mike Antonucci <mike@praxishealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Aug 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CS Handoff: Modeling scope & token footprint for Praxis Health

Elena —

Got it, thanks for the product spec and the traffic snapshot. Summary of decisions and immediate actions:
- Shortlist confirmed for POC: Mistral-7B-instruct (baseline) + LlamaX-13B quantized (cost path) + Claude-2-mini for safety-critical routing.
- Context profile: primary 8k, 16k fallback for multi-doc flows.
- Token estimate (with Solutions inflation): ~529M billing tokens / month at projected peak.
- SLA targets noted: p50 300ms interactive, p95 1s for RAG.

Actions:
1) Jordan: schedule 30m alignment call (I've sent a calendar invite for Wed 08/03 at 10am PT).
2) Praxis: share last 2 weeks of anonymized request logs or a representative sample (S3 link preferred).
3) Solutions (Grace + Ben): start perf sweep on Tuesday 08/02 and share preliminary CSV outputs by EOD 08/04.
4) Security: Elena to start the SOC checklist; we'll loop in security_eng@redwood.ai if any controls require architecture changes.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (updated), example_prompt_samples.txt, praxis_product_api_spec.pdf.

If that lines up, I'll move the MA plan to the shared Drive and kick off the perf sweep.

Best —
Jordan Blake
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
